### Page note: https://www.nfl.com/standings/tie-breaking-procedures
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
- **Publication**: “NFL Tiebreaking Procedures” – published 2019‑04‑23.  
- **Purpose**: Outline the rules used to resolve record ties in the National Football League (NFL) for playoff qualification, schedule determination, and draft order.  
- **Key Sections and Rules**  
  1. *To Break A Tie Within A Division* (Two Clubs)  
     - **Step 1** – Head‑to‑head (best won‑lost‑tied percentage in games between the clubs).  
     - **Step 2** – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in games played within the division.  
     - **Step 3** – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in common games.  
     - **Step 4** – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in games played within the conference.  
     - **Step 5** – Strength of victory in all games.  
     - **Step 6** – Strength of schedule in all games.  
     - **Step 7** – Best combined ranking among conference teams in points scored and points allowed in all games.  
     - **Step 8** – Best combined ranking among all teams in points scored and points allowed in all games.  
     - **Step 9** – Best net points in common games.  
     - **Step 10** – Best net points in all games.  
     - **Step 11** – Best net touchdowns in all games.  
     - **Step 12** – Coin toss.  
  2. *To Break A Tie Within A Division* (Three or More Clubs)  
     - **Step 1** – Head‑to‑head (best won‑lost‑tied percentage in games among the clubs).  
     - **Step 2** – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in games played within the division.  
     - **Step 3** – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in common games.  
     - **Step 4** – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in games played within the conference.  
     - **Step 5** – Strength of victory in all games.  
     - **Step 6** – Strength of schedule in all games.  
     - **Step 7** – Best combined ranking among conference teams in points scored and points allowed in all games.  
     - **Step 8** – Best combined ranking among all teams in points scored and points allowed in all games.  
     - **Step 9** – Best net points in common games.  
     - **Step 10** – Best net points in all games.  
     - **Step 11** – Best net touchdowns in all games.  
     - **Step 12** – Coin toss.  
  3. *To Break A Tie For The Wild‑Card Team*  
     - Two‑club sub‑steps (1) Head‑to‑head, (2) Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in conference games, (3) Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in common games (minimum of four), (4) Strength of victory, (5) Strength of schedule, (6) Best combined ranking among conference teams, (7) Best combined ranking among all teams, (8) Best net points in conference games, (9) Best net points in all games, (10) Best net touchdowns in all games, (11) Coin toss.  
  4. *Three or More Clubs (Wild‑Card)*  
     - Step 1 – Apply division tiebreaker to eliminate all but the highest ranked club in each division.  
     - Step 2 – Head‑to‑head sweep (only if one club has beaten each of the others or lost to each).  
     - Step 3 – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in conference games.  
     - Step 4 – Best won‑lost‑tied percentage in common games (minimum of four).  
     - Step 5 – Strength of victory in all games.  
     - Step 6 – Strength of schedule in all games.  
     - Step 7 – Best combined ranking among conference teams in points scored and points allowed in all games.  
     - Step 8 – Best combined ranking among all teams in points scored and points allowed in all games.  
     - Step 9 – Best net points in conference games.  
     - Step 10 – Best net points in all games.  
     - Step 11 – Best net touchdowns in all games.  
     - Step 12 – Coin toss.  
  5. *Other Tie‑Breaking Procedures*  
     - All tied clubs revert to the first step of the applicable division or wild‑card tiebreaker after elimination of some.  
     - If tied after step 1, the procedure restarts at step 1 of the two‑ or three‑club format.  
     - A preliminary head‑to‑head note that tied clubs may have played an unequal number of games.  
- **Usage Context**: These rules are applied to determine playoff berths, regular‑season scheduling, draft order, and other competitive outcomes in the NFL.
